channel.title: International Business Times India - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from International Business Times India (ibtimes.co.in)

item.title: Rashmika Mandanna glows in red saree, flaunts sindoor; Vijay Deverakonda shines in white vesti [Reception PICS]
item.description: The wedding reception of Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna was a star-studded event with strict entry arrangements. Rashmika looked radiant in a striking red silk saree. The couple greeted the paparazzi and also posed with their family.

item.title: MacBook Neo is here, starts at Rs 69,900: Five reasons to buy Apple's most affordable MacBook
item.description: With a lower price point, strong battery life, and AI-ready performance, MacBook Neo appears aimed squarely at students, creators, and first-time Mac users looking for an entry point into the Apple ecosystem.

item.title: Fact check: US media reports of Indian ports being used for strikes on Iran baseless
item.description: As disinformation campaigns proliferate, New Delhi's proactive digital defenses could inspire similar efforts among Global South nations, fortifying collective resilience against any fake narrative.

item.title: Fresh explosions in Jerusalem, tanker hit off Kuwait, Saudi Arabia intercepts drone amid regional tensions
item.description: A tanker off the coast of Kuwait was hit by a large explosion, causing an oil spill. ran continues its missile attacks on Israel and U.S. bases, while the conflict has already claimed over 1,000 lives, including senior Iranian leaders.

item.title: Indian stock markets gain in early trade over positive Asian cues
item.description: As of 9.30 am, Sensex gained 246 points, or 0.31 per cent, to reach 79,362 and Nifty added 84 points, or 0.35 per cent, at 24,565.

item.title: Oil prices cross $83 per barrel as Middle East tensions escalate
item.description: Oil prices rose above $83 per barrel as Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz and a container ship was hit. India, with 25 days of reserves and diversified imports from Africa, Russia, and the US, is better positioned to handle supply disruptions.

item.title: Earth faces its greatest battle beyond wars: 3–4°c warming could trigger 'Hothouse Earth'
item.description: Amid global conflicts, the climate crisis worsens unnoticed. A 3–4°C rise could trigger "Hothouse Earth," bringing heatwaves, food and water shortages, and biodiversity loss. Urgent action—renewables, ecosystem protection, and public mobilisation—is needed to prevent disaster.

item.title: 'No to war': Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez stands firm against Trump, rejects U.S.–Israeli strikes on Iran
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez rejected Trump's threat to cut trade over Spain's refusal to back U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran, summing up his stance as "No to war." He warned the conflict risks millions' lives and criticized the operation for fueling global instability, drawing parallels with the 2003 U.S.-led Iraq invasion.

item.title: Precious metals surge over inflation concerns amid escalating Middle East tensions
item.description: MCX gold April futures gained 0.31 per cent to Rs 1,62,018 per 10 grams on an intra-day basis. Meanwhile MCX silver May futures gained 1.50 per cent to Rs 2,69,551 per kg.

item.title: Trump claims US "doing very well" in 'Operation Epic Fury' against Iran
item.description: US President Donald Trump said American forces are performing "15 out of 10" in the ongoing Operation Epic Fury against Iran, claiming the US military has significantly weakened Tehran's capabilities.
